newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends steady v dollar in "boring" trade.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends steady v dollar in "boring" trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended steady at 35.85/86 against the dollar on Tuesday as lack of of market moving factors prevented movement either way, dealers said.
"It's getting dull and boring," said a dealer.
"The spot rupee looks extremely uninspiring and an aimless drift in the 80s (35.80 plus level) seems likely in the near future," said a European bank in a forex commentary.
"The eventual move higher should be seen possibly later this month," the bank predicted.
But a robust rupee has proved wrong several forecasts on the extent of its depreciation made by companies and banks alike in recent months.
The Reserve Bank of India was again in the market on Tuesday, buying dollars at 35.8550, dealers said.
The forward dollar premia continued to drift reflecting the sentiment in the call money market.
The six-month annualised premium closed the day at 7.25 percent compared with the previous close of 7.23 percent.
